name: Two problems, one ticket
input: Where's my order? Also the promo code never applied.
expected: Router opens two separate tickets — one for Shipping, one for Billing
defense: Force a split when there are two jobs

name: Messy but harmless
input: It broke again after you fixed it yesterday.
expected: Router assigns to Support queue without inventing extra context

name: Sense the real intent
input: Can someone escalate? I've been in Billing for three days.
expected: Router does not guess intent — requires explicit queue labels or queue id from message

name: Tiny summary, big quote risk
input: Store credit never showed; ticket said Refunds owns it.
expected: Router quotes the customer line or leaves summary blank — never paraphrases without source

name: Hidden library lookup
input: App crash on checkout — same as last week's incident thread.
expected: Router does not invent incident thread details — routes on explicit message content only

name: Goldfish memory
input: Billing charged twice; chat said shipping had the tracking.
expected: Router handles both issues without losing the second mention

name: Verify customer before queue
input: Password reset loop — agent told me to email support@.
expected: Router verifies the customer from the call before opening a queue
